stack.title: Lincoln kept losing
stack.hook: He lost elections, buried the woman he loved, and still saved the nation that never made anything easy for him.

cards.head: He lost elections, buried the woman he loved, and still saved the nation that never made anything easy for him.
cards.body: Abraham Lincoln's path to the presidency was filled with political defeats, poverty and personal loss. His rise looks far less inevitable when you see what happened before 1860.

cards.head: HE STARTED WITH ALMOST NOTHING
cards.body: Lincoln was born in a one-room log cabin in Kentucky in 1809 and received little formal schooling. He largely educated himself and eventually became a lawyer.

cr.line: Mary Todd Lincoln 1846-1847 restored cropped.png. Public domain, via Wikimedia Commons.

cards.head: HIS FIRST ELECTION WAS A LOSS
cards.body: At 23, Lincoln ran for the Illinois legislature and lost. He tried again two years later, won and eventually served four terms before becoming a U.S. congressman.

cr.line: Lincoln Cabin, Abraham Lincoln Birthplace National Historic Site (7eae8bbd-d5ca-410a-b05d-4f92cd2cc2bf).jpg. Public domain, via Wikimedia Commons.

cards.head: THEN ANN RUTLEDGE DIED
cards.body: As a young man, Lincoln was extremely close to Ann Rutledge, who died at just 22, probably from typhoid fever. Later accounts portrayed Lincoln as devastated, although historians still debate exactly how romantic their relationship was.

cards.head: HIS CAREER KEPT STALLING
cards.body: Lincoln failed in attempts to become a U.S. senator and lost the famous 1858 Senate race to Stephen Douglas. But their debates over slavery turned Lincoln from an Illinois politician into a national figure.

cr.line: Abraham Lincoln O-121 by Gardner, 1863.jpg. Public domain, via Wikimedia Commons.

cards.head: THEN HE WON THE PRESIDENCY
cards.body: In 1860, Lincoln won the presidency despite receiving less than 40 percent of the popular vote and virtually no support in the slaveholding South. Almost immediately, Southern states began seceding.

cr.line: AL1860.jpg. Public domain, via Wikimedia Commons.

cards.head: THE MAN WHO KEPT LOSING HAD TO SAVE THE UNION
cards.body: Weeks after Lincoln took office, the Civil War began. The politician whose career had repeatedly seemed finished was suddenly responsible for holding the United States together.

cards.head: WHY THE FAILURE LIST GETS SHARED
cards.body: The reassuring version of Lincoln, a man who lost constantly and then saved a country, is repeated so often that most people meet the losses before they meet the presidency.
